items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: So he asked me, he said, "Why don't you come on and hook up with me, and switch the tenor?"

ctx.x: Hawkins. They had a great group. They had Sir Charles Thompson on piano, and Oscar Pettiford playing the bass, and Denzil Best on drums. And they came to work at Billy Berg's. So Howard decided to stay here when the band finished the engagement. So he was searching around, trying to find a tenor saxophone player that he liked, and he couldn't find anybody he liked. So he asked me, he said, "Why don't you come on and hook up with me, and switch the tenor?" And I had never thought about playing tenor saxophone...…

I went for it because I knew that he was in the vein closer to what I really wanted to be into. It was like another milestone in my career, because I had to learn all of his library, and making the transition from the alto to the tenor. Because your ear doesn't hear the same on alto and the tenor, unless you're playing them both -- then you can hear them both. But your ear is used to hearing the notes in a certain position, a fourth away, and it takes a little time to get used to hearing it.

items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: I had Red Callender and Teddy Edwards...who else did I have...?

ctx.x: Billy Berg's?" I said, "Not particularly, no. I played there. I just come out of there. I've been there eight weeks. Now I'm going down to San Diego. I'm going to play for..." I can't think of the lady's name; "I'm going to play for her."
So I went down to... I had Red Callender and Teddy Edwards...who else did I have...? A cat named Monk played drums, I think. So anyway, we went down to San Diego...
Had you met Red Callender and Teddy Edwards when you got out to the Coast?
